**Aaron James Judge** (born April 26, 1992) is an American professional [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball") [right fielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_fielder "Right fielder") for the [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees") of [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") (MLB). He is an eight-time [MLB All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "Major League Baseball All-Star Game") and three-time [American League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_League "American League") (AL) [Most Valuable Player Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award") (MVP) winner. He holds the AL record for most [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run") in a season with 62. He stands 6 feet 7 inches (2.01 m) tall and weighs 282 pounds (128 kg), making him one of the tallest and largest players in MLB.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-1) He is considered to be among the best power hitters of all time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-3)
Judge played [college baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_baseball "College baseball") for the [Fresno State Bulldogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno_State_Bulldogs_baseball "Fresno State Bulldogs baseball"), and was selected by the Yankees with the 32nd pick in the first round of the [2013 MLB draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Major_League_Baseball_draft "2013 Major League Baseball draft"). After making his MLB debut in 2016, Judge won AL [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AL_Rookie_of_the_Year "AL Rookie of the Year") in 2017 by unanimous vote and finished second in AL MVP voting. He hit an AL-leading 52 home runs, temporarily setting a new MLB rookie record, and became the first rookie to win the [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Run_Derby_\(Major_League_Baseball\) "Home Run Derby \(Major League Baseball\)"). In 2022, Judge won his first MVP after setting the AL single-season home run record, breaking the 61-year-old mark held by [Roger Maris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Maris "Roger Maris").
Following the 2022 season, Judge re-signed with the Yankees on a nine-year, $360-million contract and was named the team's [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_New_York_Yankees_captains "List of New York Yankees captains"). In 2024, he won his second MVP by unanimous vote, leading MLB in home runs and [OPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-base_plus_slugging "On-base plus slugging") while becoming the fastest MLB player to reach 300 career home runs. That [postseason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_MLB_postseason "2024 MLB postseason"), the Yankees won their first [AL pennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_ALCS "2024 ALCS") in 15 years, but lost in the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Series "2024 World Series"). He won his third MVP and second consecutive in 2025, and also captured his first [batting title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Major_League_Baseball_batting_champions "List of Major League Baseball batting champions"). Judge captained the [United States national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_baseball_team "United States national baseball team") during the [2026 World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Baseball_Classic "2026 World Baseball Classic").
## Early life
Judge was born on April 26, 1992, in [Sacramento, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento,_California "Sacramento, California").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-4) He was adopted one day later by Patty and Wayne Judge, who both worked as teachers in nearby [Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linden,_California "Linden, California").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-fresnostatebio-5) He has an older brother, John, who was also adopted.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-6) Judge is [biracial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biracial "Biracial").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-7) Growing up, Judge was a [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants") fan.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-8) He attended [Linden High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linden_High_School_\(California\) "Linden High School \(California\)"), where he was a three-sport star.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-9) Judge played as a [pitcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitcher "Pitcher") and [first baseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_baseman "First baseman") for the baseball team, a [wide receiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_receiver "Wide receiver") for the [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") team, and as a [center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_\(basketball\) "Center \(basketball\)") for the [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") team.
As a sophomore, Judge earned All-Mother Lode League honors in varsity baseball as a first baseman.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-10) The following year, he was named the Mother Lode League's Most Outstanding Player in basketball after leading Linden to its first league title since 1986.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-LedgerDispatch-11) As a senior, he was selected as Linden High School's Athlete of the Year and received team and Mother Lode League MVP honors in all three sports, while also being named to [_The Record's_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Record_\(Stockton,_California\) "The Record \(Stockton, California\)") All-Area first team for each.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-LedgerDispatch-11) Judge set school records for single-season receiving yards (969) and touchdown receptions (17), and led the basketball team in scoring at 18.2 [points per game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_per_game "Points per game") while shooting 56% from the [field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_goal_percentage "Field goal percentage") and averaging 12.8 [rebounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebound_\(basketball\) "Rebound \(basketball\)") and 2.3 [blocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_\(basketball\) "Block \(basketball\)"), earning Cal-Hi Sports Division IV all-state recognition. In baseball, he captured the Mother Lode League's [Triple Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_Crown_\(baseball\) "Triple Crown \(baseball\)") by hitting .500 with seven home runs and 32 [RBIs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_batted_in "Run batted in"), and he dominated on the mound as well, going 6–0 with a 0.88 [ERA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_run_average "Earned run average") and 65 [strikeouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeout "Strikeout"), helping lead Linden to a league championship and a berth in the [California Interscholastic Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Interscholastic_Federation "California Interscholastic Federation") Division III playoffs.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-14)
Judge graduated from Linden High in 2010.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-16) He was the sole inductee into the Linden Athletic Hall of Fame in 2019.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-17)
## College career
Several colleges recruited Judge to play [tight end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tight_end "Tight end") in [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football"), including [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_football "Notre Dame Fighting Irish football"), [Stanford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_Cardinal_football "Stanford Cardinal football"), and [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA_Bruins_football "UCLA Bruins football"), but he preferred baseball.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-18) The [Oakland Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Athletics "Oakland Athletics") selected him in the 31st round of the [2010 MLB draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Major_League_Baseball_draft "2010 Major League Baseball draft"). He opted to enroll at [California State University, Fresno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Fresno "California State University, Fresno"), to play for the [Bulldogs baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno_State_Bulldogs_baseball "Fresno State Bulldogs baseball") team.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-19)
In 2011, Fresno State shared the [Western Athletic Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Athletic_Conference "Western Athletic Conference") (WAC) regular season title, won the [WAC Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Athletic_Conference_baseball_tournament "Western Athletic Conference baseball tournament"), and qualified for the [NCAA Division I baseball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NCAA_Division_I_baseball_tournament "2011 NCAA Division I baseball tournament").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-21) Judge was named the WAC Freshman of the Year,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-22) earned All-WAC First Team and All-Tournament Team honors,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-WACSports-23) and was selected as a Freshman [All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-American "All-American") by [Louisville Slugger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Slugger "Louisville Slugger").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-fresnostatebio-5)
In 2012, Fresno State repeated as [WAC tournament champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Western_Athletic_Conference_baseball_tournament "2012 Western Athletic Conference baseball tournament"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-24) with Judge earning All-WAC First Team honors for the second consecutive year and another selection to the [All-Tournament Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Western_Athletic_Conference_baseball_tournament#All-Tournament_Team "2012 Western Athletic Conference baseball tournament").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-WACSports-23) He finished the season tied for second in the conference with 13 [stolen bases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stolen_base "Stolen base") and ranked fifth with 47 [runs scored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_\(baseball\) "Run \(baseball\)").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-GoBulldogs-25) He also won the 2012 College Home Run Derby.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-milb-26) That summer, he played [collegiate summer baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collegiate_summer_baseball "Collegiate summer baseball") for the [Brewster Whitecaps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brewster_Whitecaps "Brewster Whitecaps") of the [Cape Cod Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod_Baseball_League "Cape Cod Baseball League"), where he received the team's Citizenship Award for being a positive team member.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-27)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-GoBulldogs-25)
As a junior in 2013, Judge led the Bulldogs in [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run") (12), [doubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_\(baseball\) "Double \(baseball\)") (15), and [runs batted in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runs_batted_in "Runs batted in") (36), earning All-[Mountain West Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_West_Conference "Mountain West Conference") First Team honors.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-nydn-28)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-GoBulldogs-25) He was named to the all-conference team in all three of his seasons for the Bulldogs—in the WAC in his first two seasons, and the Mountain West as a junior. (The Bulldogs [joined the Mountain West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9313_Mountain_West_Conference_realignment "2010–13 Mountain West Conference realignment") in July 2012, before his junior season).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-nydn-28)
Judge was honored with a jersey retirement celebration at halftime of a [Fresno State football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno_State_Bulldogs_football "Fresno State Bulldogs football") game on November 18, 2023. The following day, the Fresno State baseball team formally retired his #29 jersey.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-30)
## Professional career
### Draft and minor leagues
The Yankees drafted Judge in the first round of the [2013 MLB draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Major_League_Baseball_draft "2013 Major League Baseball draft") with the 32nd overall selection,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-32) a pick the team received as compensation after losing [Nick Swisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Swisher "Nick Swisher") in free agency.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-33) Judge signed with the Yankees and received a $1.8 million [signing bonus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signing_bonus "Signing bonus").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-34) He tore a [quadriceps femoris muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadriceps_femoris_muscle "Quadriceps femoris muscle") while participating in a [base running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_running "Base running") drill, which kept him out of the 2013 season.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-milb-26)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-35)
Judge made his professional debut with the [Charleston RiverDogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston_RiverDogs "Charleston RiverDogs") of the [Class A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_A_\(baseball\) "Class A \(baseball\)") [South Atlantic League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Atlantic_League "South Atlantic League") in 2014.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-milb-26) He had a .333 [batting average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batting_average_\(baseball\) "Batting average \(baseball\)") (6th in the league), .428 [on-base percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-base_percentage "On-base percentage") (OBP; 3rd), .530 [slugging percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slugging_percentage "Slugging percentage") (SLG; 6th), a .958 [on-base plus slugging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-base_plus_slugging "On-base plus slugging") (OPS) and hit nine home runs with 45 RBIs in 65 games for Charleston.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-36) The Yankees promoted him to the [Tampa Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Yankees "Tampa Yankees") of the [Class A-Advanced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_A-Advanced "Class A-Advanced") [Florida State League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_League "Florida State League") in June,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:7-37) where he hit .283 with a .411 OBP (2nd in the league), .442 SLG, eight home runs, and 33 RBIs in 66 games for Tampa.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-nydn-28)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-38) After the season, he played for the [Scottsdale Scorpions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsdale_Scorpions "Scottsdale Scorpions") in the [Arizona Fall League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Fall_League "Arizona Fall League"), batting .278 with four home runs in 24 games.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:7-37)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Aaron_Judge_spring_training_2015_osceola.jpg/250px-Aaron_Judge_spring_training_2015_osceola.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_spring_training_2015_osceola.jpg)Judge during Yankees' spring training in 2015
The Yankees invited Judge to [spring training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_training "Spring training") as a non-roster player in 2015.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-39) He began the season with the [Trenton Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trenton_Thunder "Trenton Thunder") of the [Double-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-A_\(baseball\) "Double-A \(baseball\)") [Eastern League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_League_\(1938%E2%80%932020\) "Eastern League \(1938–2020\)").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-40) After posting a .284/.350/.510 [slash line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slash_line "Slash line") with 12 home runs (tied for 9th in the league) in 63 games for Trenton, the Yankees promoted Judge to the [Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scranton/Wilkes-Barre_RailRiders "Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders") of the [Triple-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple-A_\(baseball\) "Triple-A \(baseball\)") [International League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_League "International League") in June.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-42) He was chosen to play in the 2015 [All-Star Futures Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Futures_Game "All-Star Futures Game").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-43) The Yankees did not include Judge in their [September call-ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_call-up "September call-up").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-44) Judge batted .224/.308/.373 with eight home runs in 61 games for Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-45)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:7-37) The Yankees invited Judge to spring training in 2016, and he returned to Triple-A to began the season. Judge was named to the International League All-Star Team in 2016 but did not play in the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple-A_All-Star_Game "Triple-A All-Star Game") after he spent a month on the disabled list due to a knee sprain.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-47) In 93 games for the RailRiders, Judge batted .270/.366/.489 with 19 home runs (4th in the league), 62 runs (tied for 8th), and 65 RBIs (tied for 7th).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-49)
### New York Yankees (2016–present)
#### 2016
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Aaron_Judge_on_September_8%2C_2016.jpg/250px-Aaron_Judge_on_September_8%2C_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_on_September_8,_2016.jpg)Judge batting in 2016
Judge made his MLB debut on August 13, 2016, starting in [right field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_fielder "Right fielder") against the [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Tampa_Bay_Rays_season "2016 Tampa Bay Rays season").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-50) In his [first MLB at-bat, Judge hit a home run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Major_League_Baseball_players_with_a_home_run_in_their_first_major_league_at_bat "List of Major League Baseball players with a home run in their first major league at bat") off [Matt Andriese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Andriese "Matt Andriese"); the previous batter, [Tyler Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Austin "Tyler Austin"), also making his MLB debut, had done the same. This marked the first time that two teammates had hit home runs in their first MLB career at-bats in the same game.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-51) Judge also hit a home run in his second MLB game, becoming the second Yankees player, after [Joe Lefebvre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lefebvre "Joe Lefebvre") in 1980, to homer in each of his first two MLB games.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-o644-52) In his debut season, Judge played in 27 games and batted .179/.263/.345 with 15 hits, four home runs, two doubles and 10 runs batted in and he struck out 42 times in 95 plate appearances.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-53) His season ended prematurely when he was placed on the 15-day disabled list with a grade two right [oblique strain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oblique_strain "Oblique strain") on September 13, 2016.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-b166-54) The Yankees missed the 2016 postseason.
#### 2017: Rookie of the Year
The Yankees named Judge their [Opening Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_Day "Opening Day") right fielder against the [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Tampa_Bay_Rays_season "2017 Tampa Bay Rays season").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-55) He had his first multi-home run game on April 28 against the [Baltimore Orioles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Baltimore_Orioles_season "2017 Baltimore Orioles season") to help the Yankees win 14–11, coming back from a 9–1 deficit.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-56) One of the home runs had a measured [exit velocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exit_velocity "Exit velocity") of 119.4 miles per hour (192.2 km/h), the fastest exit velocity for a home run measured by [Statcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statcast "Statcast") since it was adopted in 2015.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-57) (This record would later be broken by teammate [Giancarlo Stanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giancarlo_Stanton "Giancarlo Stanton") on August 9, 2018, when Stanton launched a home run with an exit velocity of 121.7 miles per hour (195.9 km/h).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-autogenerated1-58)) Judge ended April with 10 home runs, tying the rookie record set by [José Abreu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Abreu_\(first_baseman\) "José Abreu \(first baseman\)") and [Trevor Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Story "Trevor Story").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-59) He was named the [American League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_League "American League")'s (AL) [Rookie of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Rookie_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Rookie of the Month Award") for April.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-mazzeo-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:5-61) In April, he had a .303 batting average, 10 home runs, 20 RBIs, and a .411 OBP in 22 games.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-mazzeo-60)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Aaron_Judge.jpg/250px-Aaron_Judge.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge.jpg)Judge with the [Yankees in 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_New_York_Yankees_season "2017 New York Yankees season")
The Yankees debuted a cheering section in the right-field seats of [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium "Yankee Stadium") on May 22. Called "The Judge's Chambers", the section spans three rows in section 104 and contains 18 seats.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-clair-63) Fans were chosen by the team to sit there and are outfitted with black robes, wigs, and foam gavels.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-clair-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-64) In a game against the [Oakland Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Oakland_Athletics_season "2017 Oakland Athletics season") on May 28, Judge hit his first career [grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_\(baseball\) "Grand slam \(baseball\)").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-65) Judge was named AL Rookie of the Month once again for May.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:5-61) In May, he had a .347 batting average, seven home runs, 17 RBIs, and a .441 OBP in 26 games.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-66)
On June 10, Judge hit a home run that had an exit velocity of 121.1 miles per hour (194.9 km/h), again setting a new record for the hardest measured by Statcast.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-67) The following day, Judge went 4-for-4 with two home runs; one of the home runs traveled 496 feet (151 m), the longest home run hit that season.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-69) On June 12, Judge was named the [AL Player of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award"). His week ended with him leading the AL in all three [Triple Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Triple_Crown "Major League Baseball Triple Crown") categories.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-70) Judge was named the [AL Player of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Month_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Month Award") for June, batting .337 with 10 home runs, 25 RBIs and a .481 OBP. His performance in June also earned him his third consecutive AL Rookie of the Month award, the longest streak since [Mike Trout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Trout "Mike Trout") won four in a row in 2012.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:5-61)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-71) Judge had a 32-game on-base streak, including reaching base in every game in June.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-72) On July 2, Judge was voted as a starting outfielder to the [MLB All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2017 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), receiving 4,488,702 votes, the most of any player in the AL.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-73)
Judge broke [Joe DiMaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_DiMaggio "Joe DiMaggio")'s record for most home runs hit by a Yankees rookie with his 30th on July 7.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-74) He became the second rookie to hit 30 home runs before the All-Star break, following [Mark McGwire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_McGwire "Mark McGwire") in 1987,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-75) and the first Yankee to do so since [Alex Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Rodriguez "Alex Rodriguez") in 2007.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-76) Before the All-Star break, Judge hit .329 with 30 home runs and 66 RBIs.
Judge won the [Home Run Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Major_League_Baseball_Home_Run_Derby "2017 Major League Baseball Home Run Derby"), besting [Minnesota Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Twins "Minnesota Twins") third baseman [Miguel Sanó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_San%C3%B3 "Miguel Sanó") 11–10 in the final round to become the first rookie to win the Derby outright.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-77) After his performance, [MLB commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioner_of_Baseball "Commissioner of Baseball") [Rob Manfred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Manfred "Rob Manfred") stated that Judge is a player "who can become the face of the game".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-78) On July 21, Judge hit a home run that almost travelled out of [Safeco Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safeco_Field "Safeco Field"). The ball was hit so hard that Statcast initially did not measure the details of the home run.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-79) (Statcast later said the home run had a 102.8 miles per hour (165.4 km/h) exit velocity but did not estimate a distance.)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-80)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Aaron_Judge_in_2017_%2836281893203%29.jpg/250px-Aaron_Judge_in_2017_%2836281893203%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_in_2017_\(36281893203\).jpg)Judge at bat in 2017
On August 16, Judge hit a 457-foot (139 m) home run at [Citi Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citi_Field "Citi Field") that reached the third deck. He also broke a record for position players by striking out in a 33rd consecutive game.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-82) On August 20, Judge tied pitcher [Bill Stoneman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Stoneman "Bill Stoneman")'s streak of striking out in 37 consecutive games.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-83)
On September 4, Judge became the first AL rookie with 100 walks in a season since [Al Rosen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Rosen "Al Rosen") in 1950, and the first MLB rookie to do so since [Jim Gilliam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Gilliam "Jim Gilliam") in 1953. On September 10, Judge walked for the 107th time, the most walks by a rookie in a season since [Ted Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Williams "Ted Williams") in 1939.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-84) During the same game, he also became the second rookie in MLB history to hit 40 home runs in a season since McGwire (1987).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-85) He joined [Babe Ruth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth") (1920), [Lou Gehrig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Gehrig "Lou Gehrig") (1927), [Joe DiMaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_DiMaggio "Joe DiMaggio") (1937) and [Mickey Mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Mantle "Mickey Mantle") (1956) as the only Yankees to hit 40 home runs in a season at age 25 or younger.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-86)
On September 25, Judge hit his 49th and 50th home runs, tying and surpassing Mark McGwire's single-season rookie home run record.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-87) On September 30, Judge hit his 52nd home run of the season and his 33rd at Yankee Stadium, surpassing [Babe Ruth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth")'s single-season record (set in 1921) for most home runs hit by a Yankees player at his home ballpark.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-88) After the conclusion of September, Judge won AL Player of the Month for the second time and Rookie of the Month for the fourth time.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:5-61)
Judge appeared in 155 games and finished the regular season [slashing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slash_line "Slash line") .284/.422/.627 with 154 hits, 52 home runs, three triples, 24 doubles, 114 [RBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_batted_in "Run batted in"), 127 walks, 11 [intentional walks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intentional_base_on_balls "Intentional base on balls") and nine stolen bases.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-89) He led the AL in home runs, runs scored (128), and walks (a major-league rookie record 127). He ranked second in the league in RBIs. He also struck out an MLB-leading 208 times,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-90) breaking the Yankees record previously set by [Curtis Granderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtis_Granderson "Curtis Granderson") in 2012[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:0-91) and a rookie record previously set by [Kris Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Bryant "Kris Bryant") in 2015.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-92)
With the Yankees finishing the year with a 91–71 record, the team clinched a [Wild Card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Wild_Card "Major League Baseball Wild Card") in the [postseason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Major_League_Baseball_postseason "2017 Major League Baseball postseason"). During the [Wild Card Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_AL_Wild_Card_Game "2017 AL Wild Card Game") against the [Minnesota Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Minnesota_Twins_season "2017 Minnesota Twins season"), Judge hit a home run en route to an 8–4 Yankees victory.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-93) In Game 3 of the [AL Division Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_American_League_Division_Series "2017 American League Division Series") (ALDS), Judge robbed [Francisco Lindor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Lindor "Francisco Lindor") of a home run, preserving the tie game. Judge struck out 16 times in the series, setting an ALDS record.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-94) After the Yankees defeated the [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians") in the ALDS, Judge hit three home runs for the Yankees in the [AL Championship Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_American_League_Championship_Series "2017 American League Championship Series") (ALCS). He also robbed [Yulieski Gurriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yulieski_Gurriel "Yulieski Gurriel") of a potential home run in the Yankees' Game 7 ALCS loss to the [Houston Astros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Houston_Astros_season "2017 Houston Astros season"). He finished with 27 strikeouts in the postseason, a major league record at the time.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-95)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-97)
End-of-season awards for Judge included selection as an outfielder on _[Baseball America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_America "Baseball America")_ 's All-MLB Team,[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-98) the [Players Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Players_Choice_Awards "Players Choice Awards") for Outstanding AL Rookie, and a [Silver Slugger Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Slugger_Award "Silver Slugger Award").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-99) Judge was unanimously voted as the [AL Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "Major League Baseball Rookie of the Year Award").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-e037-100) He went on to finish second in the voting for the [AL Most Valuable Player Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award") to [Jose Altuve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Altuve "Jose Altuve"), receiving two out of 30 first place votes.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-101)
On November 21, it was revealed that Judge had undergone arthroscopic surgery in his left shoulder for a cartilage cleanup, an injury dating back to April of that year.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-102)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-103)
#### 2018
On March 31, Judge made his first career start at [center field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_fielder "Center fielder") in the majors. At 6 feet 7 inches (2.01 m) tall and weighing 282 pounds (128 kg), he became the tallest and heaviest player in baseball history to play the position.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-104)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-105)
Batting .277 with 25 home runs and 58 RBIs, Judge was named a starting outfielder for the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2018 Major League Baseball All-Star Game").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-106) Judge hit a solo home run off [National League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_League_\(baseball\) "National League \(baseball\)") starter [Max Scherzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Scherzer "Max Scherzer").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-107)
On July 26, a 93 mph fastball by [Kansas City Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Royals "Kansas City Royals") pitcher [Jakob Junis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakob_Junis "Jakob Junis") hit Judge on his right wrist and he left the game. Later, an [MRI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_resonance_imaging "Magnetic resonance imaging")/[CT scan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CT_scan "CT scan") revealed that he suffered a fractured [ulnar styloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulnar_styloid_process "Ulnar styloid process") bone in his wrist. No surgery was required, and initial reports gave a three-week timetable for Judge to recover.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-108) The injury took longer to heal than expected, with Judge missing close to two months. On September 18, Judge returned to the starting lineup.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-109) He finished the season with a .278 batting average, 27 home runs, and 67 RBIs in 112 games.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-110) The Yankees beat the [Oakland Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Athletics "Oakland Athletics") in the [Wild Card Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Major_League_Baseball_postseason#\(4\)_New_York_Yankees_vs._\(5\)_Oakland_Athletics "2018 Major League Baseball postseason")[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-111) but were defeated, three games to one, by the Red Sox in the [ALDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Major_League_Baseball_postseason#\(1\)_Boston_Red_Sox_vs._\(4\)_New_York_Yankees "2018 Major League Baseball postseason").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-112)
#### 2019
[![Aaron Judge holding a bat, wearing a batting helmet and warmup top](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Aaron_Judge_at_Camden_Yards_4-4-19%2846816281264%29.jpg/250px-Aaron_Judge_at_Camden_Yards_4-4-19%2846816281264%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_at_Camden_Yards_4-4-19\(46816281264\).jpg)Judge during batting practice in 2019
Judge started the season off with a .288 batting average, five home runs, and 11 RBIs in his first 20 games.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-113) However, on April 20, Judge suffered a left [oblique strain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oblique_strain "Oblique strain") while hitting a single in the sixth inning against the [Kansas City Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Royals "Kansas City Royals").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-blum-114) He did not play again until June 21.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-115)
On August 27, Judge hit his 17th home run of the season and 100th home run of his career. Coming in his 371st game, it made him the third-fastest MLB player to hit 100 home runs.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-bleacherreport1-116)
Judge hit a home run over [Fenway Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenway_Park "Fenway Park")'s [Green Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Monster "Green Monster") for the first time on September 8. With this home run, the [2019 Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_New_York_Yankees_season "2019 New York Yankees season") set a new franchise record for team home runs in a season.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-117)
In 2019, Judge batted .272/.381/.540, with 103 hits, 27 home runs, one triple,18 doubles and 55 RBIs in 447 plate appearances across 102 games.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-118) He had the fastest average exit velocity on balls hit in play among major leaguers at 95.9 mph (154.3 km/h).[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-119) He led the league in [defensive runs saved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_Runs_Saved "Defensive Runs Saved") as a right fielder (19 runs saved, tied with [Cody Bellinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Bellinger "Cody Bellinger")) but did so in fewer innings (775+1⁄3 compared to 911+1⁄3 for Bellinger). Judge earned the [Wilson Defensive Player of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Defensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award "Wilson Defensive Player of the Year Award") for his position in right field.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-120)
#### 2020
During spring training in March, Judge felt soreness in his pectoral area. It was revealed that he had suffered a [stress fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_fracture "Stress fracture") in his ribs and was shut down for at least two weeks.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-121) However, the start of the season was delayed until July.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-122)
Judge began the [shortened 2020 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Major_League_Baseball_season "2020 Major League Baseball season") with five consecutive games with a home run (6 during the span), launching a 419-feet, 108 mph three-run shot off of [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox") pitcher [Matt Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Hall_\(baseball\) "Matt Hall \(baseball\)"). His streak ended on August 3 when he went 2-for-4 without a home run. It was the longest home run streak by a Yankees player since [Alex Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Rodriguez "Alex Rodriguez") (September 4–9, 2007).[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-123) On August 14, Judge was placed on the 10-day [injured list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_list "Injured list") with a right calf strain.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-124) On August 26, he was again placed on the 10-day injured list after straining the same calf the day he returned against the [Atlanta Braves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-125) He finished the season slashing .257/.336/.554 with 26 hits, nine home runs, three doubles and 22 RBIs over 28 games.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-126) In the playoffs, he batted 4-for-30 with 3 home runs and 5 RBI as the Yankees lost to Tampa Bay in the [ALDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_American_League_Division_Series "2020 American League Division Series").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-127)
#### 2021
During the week of May 10–16, Judge earned his fourth career [AL Player of the Week Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award").[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-128) Judge had a [slash line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slash_line "Slash line") of .571/.640/1.333 with eight runs scored, 12 hits, a double, five home runs, six RBIs, and three walks in six games (five multi-hit games and his 13th career multi-homer game). He also hit his 130th career home run, the second-most in MLB history through 460 career games, trailing only [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard "Ryan Howard") (142).[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-129) On May 23, Judge recorded his first career walk-off RBI, taking a walk on a 3–1 pitch from [Liam Hendriks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Hendriks "Liam Hendriks") of the [Chicago White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox "Chicago White Sox").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-130)
On July 9, Judge recorded his 500th career hit during a game against the [Houston Astros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Astros "Houston Astros") by hitting a double to left field off pitcher [Brandon Bielak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Bielak "Brandon Bielak").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-131) He became the second-fastest Yankee to 500 hits and 100 home runs. He accomplished the feat in his 506th game, with only [Joe DiMaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_DiMaggio "Joe DiMaggio") getting there faster, at 395 games.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-132)
Judge was named the starting right fielder in the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2021 Major League Baseball All-Star Game").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-133) Following the All-Star Game, Judge was placed on the [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_sports "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports") injured list after testing positive for the virus.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-134) Judge returned against the [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Rays "Tampa Bay Rays") on July 27.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-135)
On August 12, in the [Field of Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_of_Dreams "Field of Dreams") [game in Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_at_Field_of_Dreams "MLB at Field of Dreams"), Judge hit two multiple-run home runs.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-136) He also hit two home runs on September 11 against the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets "New York Mets") with his 31st and 32nd home runs.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-137) On October 3, the last game of the regular season, Judge recorded his first career [walk-off hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk-off_hit "Walk-off hit"), a single that scored [Tyler Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Wade "Tyler Wade") to beat Tampa Bay 1–0 and clinch a [Wild Card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Wild_Card "Major League Baseball Wild Card") spot for the Yankees.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-138) In the [Wild Card Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_American_League_Wild_Card_Game "2021 American League Wild Card Game"), Judge became the first Yankee to be ruled out at home plate on a hit in a winner-take-all game.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-139)
Judge finished the 2021 season batting .287/.373/.544 with 158 hits, 39 home runs, 24 doubles, 98 [RBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_batted_in "Run batted in"), 75 walks, two [intentional walks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intentional_base_on_balls "Intentional base on balls"), and six [stolen bases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stolen_base "Stolen base").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-140) After the season, Judge won a [Fielding Bible Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_Bible_Award "Fielding Bible Award") for his defensive excellence and his second [Silver Slugger Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Slugger_Award "Silver Slugger Award").[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-141) On November 23, Judge was named to the First Team of the [All-MLB Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-MLB_Team "All-MLB Team") as an outfielder.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-142) He finished fourth in AL MVP voting.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-143)
#### 2022: AL home run record, MVP
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Judge_home_run.jpg/250px-Judge_home_run.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Judge_home_run.jpg)Judge (near third base) circles the bases at [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium "Yankee Stadium") after his first home run of the 2022 season.
Before the [2022 Yankees season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_New_York_Yankees_season "2022 New York Yankees season"), Judge and the Yankees were unsuccessful in negotiating a long-term contract. [General manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_manager_\(baseball\) "General manager \(baseball\)") [Brian Cashman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Cashman "Brian Cashman") told [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") that the team offered Judge $17 million in arbitration and a seven-year extension worth $213.5 million.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-espn-2022-04-144) Judge avoided [salary arbitration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pendulum_arbitration "Pendulum arbitration") and signed a one-year, $19 million contract on June 24, with additional $250,000 bonuses for winning each of the MVP Award and the [World Series MVP Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Series_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "World Series Most Valuable Player Award").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-cbsnews-2022-06-24-145)
Judge slashed .293/.361/.600 with six home runs in April.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BR2022-146) He hit his first career [walk-off home run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk-off_home_run "Walk-off home run") on May 10 off [Toronto Blue Jays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Blue_Jays "Toronto Blue Jays") [closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(baseball\) "Closer \(baseball\)") [Jordan Romano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Romano "Jordan Romano").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-147) Judge won the AL Player of the Month Award for May.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PotM-148) During the month, Judge slashed .311/.378/.699 with 12 home runs.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BR2022-146) He hit his second walk-off home run on June 26 against the [Houston Astros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Astros "Houston Astros").[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-Hoch2022-149)
Judge was elected as a starter for the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2022 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), receiving the most fan votes of any player in the AL.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-150) This was his second consecutive and fourth overall All-Star selection.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-151)
Judge slugged his third walk-off homer for the season against the visiting [Kansas City Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Royals "Kansas City Royals") on July 28, tying [Mickey Mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Mantle "Mickey Mantle") for most by a Yankee in a season.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-152)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-153) Judge won back-to-back [AL Player of the Week Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Player_of_the_Week_Award "Major League Baseball Player of the Week Award") for the weeks ending July 24 and 31.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PotW-154) Judge also claimed the AL Player of the Month Award for July after batting .333/.436/.806 with 13 home runs.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PotM-148)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BR2022-146)
On July 30, Judge became the second-fastest player in MLB history to hit 200 home runs (behind [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard "Ryan Howard")), launching a two-run shot off of [Jon Heasley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Heasley "Jon Heasley") of the Kansas City Royals.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-155) On August 29, during a game against the [Los Angeles Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Angels "Los Angeles Angels"), Judge hit his 50th home run for the season, coming off reliever [Ryan Tepera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Tepera "Ryan Tepera"). He became only the tenth player in MLB history and third player in Yankees franchise history to record multiple [50 home run seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_home_run_club "50 home run club").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-'Just_another_number':_Yanks'_Judge-156)
Judge hit his 55th home run during the first game of a doubleheader against the [Minnesota Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Twins "Minnesota Twins") on September 7 off rookie starting pitcher [Louie Varland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louie_Varland "Louie Varland"). He became the fourth player in MLB history to hit at least 55 home runs and steal at least 15 bases in a season, joining [Babe Ruth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth") (1921), [Sammy Sosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Sosa "Sammy Sosa") (1998), and [Ken Griffey Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Griffey_Jr. "Ken Griffey Jr.") (1997–98).[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-157) On September 18 against the [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers"), Judge equaled [Hank Greenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Greenberg "Hank Greenberg") and Sosa's record of 11 multiple home run games in an MLB season, hitting his 58th and 59th home runs, while also tying and surpassing Greenberg (1938) and [Jimmie Foxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmie_Foxx "Jimmie Foxx") (1932) for the AL single-season record for most home runs by a right-handed batter.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BaseballAlmanac-158)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BR2022-146) Judge's 60th home run came on September 20.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-159)
On September 28, Judge hit his 61st home run off [Tim Mayza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Mayza "Tim Mayza") of the Toronto Blue Jays, tying [Roger Maris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Maris "Roger Maris") for the most home runs in a single season in AL history.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-160) In the second game of a doubleheader (and the Yankees' second-to-last regular season game) against the [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_\(baseball\) "Texas Rangers \(baseball\)") at [Globe Life Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globe_Life_Field "Globe Life Field") on October 4, Judge hit his 62nd home run off [Jesús Tinoco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs_Tinoco "Jesús Tinoco"), setting the new single-season AL home run record.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-161)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-162)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-Waldstein-163) Judge was selected as the AL Player of the Week for the week of September 29–October 5.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-164) He claimed his third AL Player of the Month Award of the season in September.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PotM-148) He batted .417/.565/.869 for September.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BR2022-146)
In 2022, Judge led the major leagues with 62 home runs, 133 runs scored, 131 RBI (tied with [Pete Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Alonso "Pete Alonso") of the Mets), 111 walks, and batted .311/.425/.686 with 177 hits, 28 doubles, and 19 intentional walks, while stealing 16 bases in 19 attempts, in 157 games.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-auto-165) He was denied the AL [triple crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_crown_\(baseball\) "Triple crown \(baseball\)"), as [Luis Arráez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Arr%C3%A1ez "Luis Arráez") of the Minnesota Twins had a batting average that was five points higher than Judge's.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-166)
Judge won the [AL MVP Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award"), earning 28 of 30 first-place votes.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-167) He was also named to the [All-MLB Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-MLB_Team "All-MLB Team").[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-168) Judge's 2022 campaign is considered one of the best offensive seasons in major league history.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-169)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-170) On December 30, he was voted the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") (AP) "Male Athlete of the Year" by a panel of 40 sports writers and editors from news outlets throughout the United States. Judge just edged out [Los Angeles Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Angels "Los Angeles Angels") [two-way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-way_player#Baseball "Two-way player") star and 2021's winner [Shohei Ohtani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shohei_Ohtani "Shohei Ohtani") in voting.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-171)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-172) Judge was also selected as the [Time Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time \(magazine\)") Athlete of the Year.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-173)
The [Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_New_York_Yankees_season "2022 New York Yankees season") qualified for the [postseason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Major_League_Baseball_postseason "2022 Major League Baseball postseason"), facing the [Cleveland Guardians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Cleveland_Guardians_season "2022 Cleveland Guardians season") in the [ALDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_American_League_Division_Series "2022 American League Division Series"), where Judge slashed .200/.238/.500 with two home runs, as the Yankees defeated the Guardians in five games.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:4-174) In the [ALCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_American_League_Championship_Series "2022 American League Championship Series"), Judge hit just .063/.118/.063 with one hit and a walk as the Yankees were swept in four games by the [Houston Astros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Houston_Astros_season "2022 Houston Astros season"), who would go on to win the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Series "2022 World Series").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-175)
After the 2022 season, Judge became a [free agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agency_\(Major_League_Baseball\) "Free agency \(Major League Baseball\)"). The Yankees extended the [qualifying offer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qualifying_offer "Qualifying offer") of a one-year contract worth $19.65 million to Judge,[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-176) but he declined.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-177) During free agency, he was pursued by the [San Diego Padres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres") and [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants") as well as the Yankees.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-178)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-179) By early December 2022, the Padres offered Judge over $400 million, according to Judge's agent. The Yankees were only offering $320 million over eight years. A new deal with the Yankees was created in a phone call between Judge and Yankees owner [Hal Steinbrenner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hal_Steinbrenner "Hal Steinbrenner"), when Steinbrenner offered to add a ninth year and an additional $40 million.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-Aaron_Judge's_free_agency-180) That became the foundation of an agreement that the Yankees, and Judge signed on December 20, 2022, with the nine-year, $360 million deal breaking the record for the largest free agent deal in MLB history.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-181) In a press conference on the following day, Steinbrenner named Judge the 16th [captain of the Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_New_York_Yankees_team_captains "List of New York Yankees team captains") and the first since [Derek Jeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Jeter "Derek Jeter") had retired eight years earlier.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-182)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-183)
#### 2023
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Judge_2023.jpg/250px-Judge_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Judge_2023.jpg)Judge with the [Yankees in 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_New_York_Yankees_season "2023 New York Yankees season")
On 2023 MLB [Opening Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_Day "Opening Day") at [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium "Yankee Stadium"), Judge hit his first home run of the year off [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants") ace [Logan Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_Webb "Logan Webb") into [Monument Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_Park_\(Yankee_Stadium\) "Monument Park \(Yankee Stadium\)").[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-184) Judge went on the 10-day injured list after a mild hip [strain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strain_\(injury\) "Strain \(injury\)") suffered while sliding into base playing against the [Minnesota Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Twins "Minnesota Twins") at [Target Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_Field "Target Field") on April 26.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-185) Judge returned against the [Oakland Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Athletics "Oakland Athletics") on May 9.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BR2023-186)
Judge received the AL Player of the Week Award for the week of May 15–21.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-187) Despite missing the first week of games in May, Judge also won the AL Player of the Month Award for May after batting .342/.474/.882 with 12 home runs in 21 games.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-MLB2023-188)
On June 3, Judge crashed through a closed gate in the outfield wall at [Dodger Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodger_Stadium "Dodger Stadium") while recording a [fly out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fly_out "Fly out") off [JD Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Martinez "JD Martinez"),[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-189) causing a [sprain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprain "Sprain") to his toe and leading to him missing 42 games, with the Yankees going 19–23 in his absence.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-190) Despite the injury, Judge was elected to the [All Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2023 Major League Baseball All-Star Game") but was unable to participate, and he was replaced in the lineup by the [Texas Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Rangers_\(baseball\) "Texas Rangers \(baseball\)")' [Adolis Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolis_Garcia "Adolis Garcia").[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-191) Judge returned against the [Baltimore Orioles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Orioles "Baltimore Orioles") at [Camden Yards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camden_Yards "Camden Yards") on July 28.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-BR2023-186)
On August 23, Judge hit three home runs, including a grand slam, against the [Washington Nationals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Nationals "Washington Nationals") at [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium "Yankee Stadium").[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-192) He repeated the feat at home against the [Arizona Diamondbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Diamondbacks "Arizona Diamondbacks") less than a month later on September 22, becoming the first Yankee to homer three times in a game twice in a season.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-193) Judge won his second AL Player of the Week Award of the season on September 24.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-194)
On September 2, Judge hit his 250th career home run (30th of the season) off of Astros ace [Justin Verlander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Verlander "Justin Verlander") in the fifth inning. It was his 810th career game, setting a new record as the fastest player to reach 250 home runs in MLB history, passing marks previously set by [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard "Ryan Howard") (855 games) and [Ralph Kiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Kiner "Ralph Kiner") (871 games).[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-195)
Despite missing 56 games, Judge hit 37 home runs in 2023, putting him on a 55 home run pace had he played a full season. He slashed .267/.406/.613, from 106 games, his second consecutive year with an OPS over 1.000 and his third overall.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-MLBJudge2023-196) He had 98 hits, 16 doubles, 75 RBI, 88 walks, 9 [intentional walks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intentional_base_on_balls "Intentional base on balls"), and 3 stolen bases (caught stealing once).[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-MLBJudge2023-196) The [Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_New_York_Yankees_season "2023 New York Yankees season") finished the regular season in fourth place in the [AL East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AL_East "AL East") and missed the playoffs for the first time since [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_New_York_Yankees_season "2016 New York Yankees season").[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-197)
Judge received the [Roberto Clemente Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Clemente_Award "Roberto Clemente Award") before Game 3 of the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Series "2023 World Series"). The award acknowledged his exemplary character and charity work promoting responsible youth and civic citizenship in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") and [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") through his ALL RISE Foundation.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-198)[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-199) Judge was also selected to the [All-MLB Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-MLB_Team "All-MLB Team") for the third successive year, this time to the second team.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-200) He finished 15th in AL MVP voting.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-201)
As captain, Judge appeared to take a more hands-on approach towards the Yankees organization, having conversations with Steinbrenner about the team direction and potential changes following the Yankees missing the [postseason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Major_League_Baseball_postseason "2023 Major League Baseball postseason").[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-202)
#### 2024: Second MVP, AL pennant
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Aaron_Judge_%2853947419176%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Aaron_Judge_%2853947419176%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_\(53947419176\)_\(cropped\).jpg)Judge in 2024
Following an injury-interrupted spring training, Judge started the [2024 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_New_York_Yankees_season "2024 New York Yankees season") slowly, hitting .180 through the first three weeks of April.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-203)[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:1-204)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-205) Judge primarily played at center field early in the season but also made his first major league appearance in [left field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_field "Left field") when [Alex Verdugo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Verdugo "Alex Verdugo") was on paternity leave.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-206)[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-207) By late April, Judge appeared more comfortable and improved his performance at the plate, collecting eight hits and three home runs along with six walks in the final week of the month.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:1-204)
Judge was selected as the AL Player of the Week for the week of May 19, after going 10-for-20 and slugging 1.200 with three home runs and five doubles in this period.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PotW-154)[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-208) Judge was also selected as the AL Player of the Month for May, having hit 14 home runs and 12 doubles in the month, with 27 RBI, slashing .361/.479/.918.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:1-204)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:2-209) This marked Judge's seventh AL Player of the Month selection, and his third consecutive May honor.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:2-209) Judge also completed a homecoming of sorts, playing his first series at [Oracle Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Park "Oracle Park") against the [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants"), where he went 6-for-10 with three home runs and six RBI as the Yankees swept the series.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:3-210) By the end of May, Judge improved his season slash line to .277/.405/.643, with an OPS of 1.048.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-211)
For the week ending June 9, Judge received his second AL Player of the Week award for 2024.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PotW-154) In the six-game homestand split against the [Minnesota Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Twins "Minnesota Twins") and [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers"), Judge slashed .500/.630/1.200 with three home runs and 12 RBI.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-212) Following a 3-for-4 game against the Dodgers on June 9, Judge raised his season batting average to over .300 for the first time.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:3-210) At end of June, Judge led the majors in home runs (31), RBI (82), and OPS (1.144), and he was second in the AL in batting average (.316) among qualified hitters.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-213)[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-214) Judge won the AL Player of the Month Award again in June, for the second consecutive month, slashing .409/.514/.864, with 11 home runs and 37 RBI for the month.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PotM-148)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-215)
On June 27, Judge was announced as a starting outfielder for the AL in the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2024 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), having received the most votes.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-216) This was the second time in three seasons that he received the most All-Star votes.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-217)
On August 14, batting against [Chad Kuhl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Kuhl "Chad Kuhl") of the [Chicago White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox "Chicago White Sox"), Judge hit his 300th career home run in the Yankees' 10–2 victory. He became the fastest player to ever hit 300 home runs, taking him 955 games and 3,431 at-bats, surpassing both [Ralph Kiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Kiner "Ralph Kiner")'s record by 132 games and [Babe Ruth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth")'s by 400 at-bats.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:6-218)[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-219) He became the second hitter to record his 300th home run prior to his 1,000th hit.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-220) He hit his 50th and 51st home runs of the season on August 25, becoming the fifth player in MLB history with three-plus seasons of 50 or more home runs.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-221) Judge was named the AL Player of the Week for the week of August 19–25, following a strong homestand against the [Cleveland Guardians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Guardians "Cleveland Guardians") and [Colorado Rockies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rockies "Colorado Rockies").[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-b777-222) On August 26, Judge collected his 1,000th career hit, a line-drive single to right field against [José Ferrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_A._Ferrer "José A. Ferrer") at [Nationals Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationals_Park "Nationals Park").[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-c395-223) Judge received the August AL Player of the Month Award, his third monthly award of the season, after slashing .389/.530/.856.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-224)
On September 13, Judge hit a go-ahead grand slam at Yankee Stadium against the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox").[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-225) This ended a 16-game homerless streak, the longest of his major league career.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-226) Judge ended the regular season slashing .322/.458/.701, with 180 hits, 58 home runs, one triple, 36 doubles, 144 RBI, 133 walks, 20 intentional walks and 10 stolen bases from 155 games.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:3-210)
The Yankees won the [ALCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_American_League_Championship_Series "2024 American League Championship Series") against the Cleveland Guardians in five games in which Judge hit two home runs and notched five RBIs. In his first [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Series "2024 World Series"), Judge went 1-for-12 with seven strikeouts in the first three games of the series as the Yankees fell into a 3–0 series deficit.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-227)[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-228) In Game 5, Judge hit his first World Series home run as the Yankees jumped out to a 5–0 lead, but a series of defensive mistakes, including Judge's first [error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Error_\(baseball\) "Error \(baseball\)") of the year, allowed the lead to slip away as the Yankees lost the game 7–6, and thus the series in five games.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-229) After the season, Judge won the [AL MVP Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award"). He became the second Yankee player to win the award unanimously, following [Mickey Mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Mantle "Mickey Mantle") in 1956.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-230)
#### 2025: Third MVP
[![Aaron Judge following through with a swing at the plate in St. Louis](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Aaron_Judge_in_Stlouis_2025_%28cropped%29.png/250px-Aaron_Judge_in_Stlouis_2025_%28cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_in_Stlouis_2025_\(cropped\).png)Judge in 2025
On March 29, Judge hit three home runs and a double with eight RBI against the [Milwaukee Brewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Milwaukee_Brewers_season "2025 Milwaukee Brewers season"), his third career three-homer game.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-231) On March 31, Judge was named the AL Player of the Week for the opening week of the season after going 6-for-11 and slugging 1.818 with four home runs and 11 RBI.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-2025wk1-232)
On April 3, Judge hit his 500th career extra-base hit with a first-inning, three-run home run off the [Arizona Diamondbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Arizona_Diamondbacks_season "2025 Arizona Diamondbacks season")' [Merrill Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merrill_Kelly "Merrill Kelly"). Judge became the third-fastest Yankee to reach the milestone in terms of games played, having done so in his 999th game.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-233) In the same game, Judge became the first player in MLB history with five home runs and 15 RBI in his team's first six games of the season.
