On April 4 against the [Pittsburgh Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Pittsburgh_Pirates_season "2025 Pittsburgh Pirates season"), playing in his 1,000th game for the Yankees, Judge registered his 321st home run, equaling Babe Ruth's record for home runs in his first 1,000 Yankees games.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:9-234) By the end of April, Judge was slashing .427/.521/.761 with 10 home runs and 32 RBI.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-235) Judge won with the AL Player of the Month Award for April, the tenth of his career.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:10-236) On May 30 against the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "2025 Los Angeles Dodgers season"), Judge and [Shohei Ohtani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shohei_Ohtani "Shohei Ohtani") became the first reigning MVPs ever to each hit a home run in the first inning of the same game.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-237) Judge was named the AL Player of the Month again in May, after slashing .364/.453/.798, with 11 home runs on the month. His 11th career monthly award is the most in AL history, surpassing [Alex Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Rodriguez "Alex Rodriguez").[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-238)[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:10-236)
On June 26, Judge was announced as a starting outfielder for the AL in the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game "2025 Major League Baseball All-Star Game"), having received the most votes for the third time in four seasons and the second straight year.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-239)[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-240) On July 12, Judge hit his 350th career home run against the [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Chicago_Cubs_season "2025 Chicago Cubs season"); he accomplished this in 1,088 games, breaking the record of 1,280 games by [Mark McGwire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_McGwire "Mark McGwire").[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:11-241) On July 27, Judge was placed on the 10-day injury list with a flexor strain in his right elbow, following discomfort while throwing from the outfield against the [Toronto Blue Jays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Blue_Jays "Toronto Blue Jays").[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-242) He was reactivated on August 5, mostly appearing as designated hitter in the following month, before making more regular appearances in the outfield from mid-September.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-243) On September 9 against the [Detroit Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Detroit_Tigers_season "2025 Detroit Tigers season"), Judge hit his 359th home run, passing [Yogi Berra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yogi_Berra "Yogi Berra") for fifth place on the Yankees all-time home run list.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-244)
On September 11, two more home runs against the Tigers brought his total to 361, tying Joe DiMaggio for fourth all-time in Yankees history.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-Tied_for_4th-245) The next day, he passed DiMaggio with his 362nd against the Red Sox.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-PassesDiMaggio-246) This was his 19th first-inning home run of the season, breaking a tie with Alex Rodriguez (2001) and his own mark from 2024 for the most home runs by a player in a single inning in a season.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-1st_inning-247) On September 15, Judge was named the AL Player of the Week after going 9-for-20 with a 1.760 OPS, five home runs, and five RBI.[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-2025wk25-248) On September 24, he hit two home runs against the [Chicago White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Chicago_White_Sox_season "2025 Chicago White Sox season"), bringing him to the 50 home run mark in a season for the fourth time, tying [Babe Ruth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth"), [Mark McGwire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_McGwire "Mark McGwire"), and [Sammy Sosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Sosa "Sammy Sosa") for the most such seasons in MLB history. Judge and Ruth are the only Yankees to have consecutive years of 50 or more homers.[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-50_homer_club-249) On September 29, Judge was named the AL Player of the Week after going 9-for-20 with four home runs, nine RBI and an OPS of 1.693.[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-2025wk26-250) He also won the AL Player of the Month for September after slashing .391/.440/.772 with 10 home runs.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-251)
Judge finished the regular season with a .331 batting average, leading the major leagues, and winning his first career [batting title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Major_League_Baseball_batting_champions "List of Major League Baseball batting champions"). At 6 feet 7 inches, he became the tallest batting champion in MLB history.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-252) He slashed .331/.457/.688 with 53 home runs, 179 hits, two triples, 30 doubles, 114 RBI, 124 walks, 36 intentional walks, and 12 stolen bases in 152 games.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-253) His 53 home runs were the most ever by a batting champion.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-254) Judge's 36 intentional walks broke the AL single-season record, overtaking [Ted Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Williams "Ted Williams")' record of 34 set in the [1957 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_Boston_Red_Sox_season "1957 Boston Red Sox season").[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-255)
In the [AL Wild Card Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_American_League_Wild_Card_Series "2025 American League Wild Card Series") against the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Boston_Red_Sox_season "2025 Boston Red Sox season"), Judge went 4-for-11 with one walk and one RBI.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-256) On October 7 at Yankee Stadium, with the Yankees facing being swept in the [AL Division Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_American_League_Division_Series "2025 American League Division Series") by the [Toronto Blue Jays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Toronto_Blue_Jays_season "2025 Toronto Blue Jays season"), Judge went 3-for-4 and hit the tying three-run home run off the foul pole as the Yankees came back from a 6–1 run deficit to keep the series alive.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-257) This effort answered some of the lingering criticism of his previously underwhelming postseason performances, which had amplified after he had struck out with the bases loaded in the series opener.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-258) Judge ended the postseason slashing .500/.581/.692 with 13 hits, one home run, two doubles and seven RBI across seven games as the Yankees were eliminated by the Blue Jays in four games.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-259)
Judge won his third career and second consecutive AL MVP award. In a tight race, Judge received 17 first-place votes, four more than [Cal Raleigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cal_Raleigh "Cal Raleigh").[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-260)[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-261)

## International career
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Aaron_Judge_on_being_named_captain_of_Team_USA_%28Os0w_J0XHEE%29.png/250px-Aaron_Judge_on_being_named_captain_of_Team_USA_%28Os0w_J0XHEE%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_on_being_named_captain_of_Team_USA_\(Os0w_J0XHEE\).png)Judge (left) being announced as captain of the [United States national baseball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_baseball_team "United States national baseball team") ahead of the [2026 World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Baseball_Classic "2026 World Baseball Classic") during a press conference with [Mark DeRosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_DeRosa "Mark DeRosa") in April 2025
Judge did not compete in the [2023 World Baseball Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Baseball_Classic "2023 World Baseball Classic") (WBC), choosing instead to focus on preparing for his season with the Yankees, given his recent contract and captaincy.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-271)
On April 14, 2025, Judge was named captain of [Team USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_national_baseball_team "United States national baseball team") ahead of the [2026 WBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Baseball_Classic "2026 World Baseball Classic"). Manager [Mark DeRosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_DeRosa "Mark DeRosa") announced the decision on [MLB Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_Network "MLB Network"), with Judge joining the broadcast to express his excitement: "Now, getting a chance to have 'USA' across my chest and represent all the great people in our country and represent what this country means, it's a great opportunity. I never had this opportunity before, even growing up as a kid, so I'm definitely looking forward to it."[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-272)
At the WBC, Judge posted a slash line of .222/.364/.481, slugging two home runs with five RBIs and six hits across seven games.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-273) Highlights included homering on his very first swing of the tournament — a 405-foot, 106.5 mph two-run blast against [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_baseball_team "Brazil national baseball team") — and a pair of standout defensive plays from right field, throwing out runners attempting to advance to third base.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-274) He threw out [Joey Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Ortiz "Joey Ortiz") against [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_baseball_team "Mexico national baseball team") in pool play, then did the same to [Fernando Tatis Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Tat%C3%ADs_Jr. "Fernando Tatís Jr.") against the [Dominican Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Republic_national_baseball_team "Dominican Republic national baseball team") in the semi-final game with his throw clocked at 95.7 mph.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-275)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-276)
Judge and Team USA advanced to the championship game against [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela_national_baseball_team "Venezuela national baseball team"), but fell short by a score of 3–2, marking back-to-back runner-up finishes for the U.S. in the WBC. The offense for the U.S. went quiet in the game, with Judge going 0-for-4 with three strikeouts.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-277)
## Player profile
Judge is listed at 6 feet 7 inches (2.01 m) and 282 pounds (128 kg).[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-278) Due to his large size and strength, he has elicited comparisons to teammate [Giancarlo Stanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giancarlo_Stanton "Giancarlo Stanton"), as well as former MLB players [Richie Sexson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Sexson "Richie Sexson"),[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-279) [Dave Winfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Winfield "Dave Winfield"), and [Willie Stargell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Stargell "Willie Stargell").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-nydn-28)
His power output is historically significant: he is one of only eight players in [MLB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") history to record an [OPS+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-base_plus_slugging#Adjusted_OPS_\(OPS+\) "On-base plus slugging") above 200 in three seasons.[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-280)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-auto-165) He is also one of just 14 players in MLB history to [slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slugging_percentage "Slugging percentage") above .700 in a season with a minimum of 550 [plate appearances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plate_appearance "Plate appearance").[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-281) He is the fourth player ever to produce four seasons with 50 or more [home runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run "Home run"), alongside Ruth, [Sammy Sosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Sosa "Sammy Sosa"), and [Mark McGwire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_McGwire "Mark McGwire").[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-282) Since [Statcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statcast "Statcast") began tracking exit velocity in 2015, Judge broke the record for the hardest-hit home run with a 121.1 mph blast on June 10, 2017, against the [Baltimore Orioles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Orioles "Baltimore Orioles"); although later surpassed, it ranked fifth as of 2025.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-283) Judge and [Miguel Sanó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_San%C3%B3 "Miguel Sanó") are the only MLB players since 2015 to hit multiple home runs measuring at least 495 feet.[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-284)
### Pregame rituals
Judge has been credited as a team leader both on and off the field.[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-285)
He has a number of rituals before, during, and after games. According to [Michael Kay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Kay_\(sports_broadcaster\) "Michael Kay \(sports broadcaster\)") (as discussed during _[The Michael Kay Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Michael_Kay_Show "The Michael Kay Show")_), before each game at Yankee Stadium, Judge ceremoniously tosses exactly 40 sunflower seeds in the grass behind home plate (one for each man on the Yankees [extended roster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40-man_roster "40-man roster").)[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-espn.com-286) The prayer he recites after he tosses the seeds is unknown to the public.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-espn.com-286)
During his 2017 rookie season, Judge kept a note on his phone that read ".179", his batting average with the Yankees in 2016, and looked at it daily as a source of motivation.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-287)
### Uniform
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/Aaron_Judge_July_23%2C_2020_%2850145941858%29.jpg/250px-Aaron_Judge_July_23%2C_2020_%2850145941858%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaron_Judge_July_23,_2020_\(50145941858\).jpg)Judge chasing down a fly ball
Judge has worn the unusual [uniform number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_number_\(Major_League_Baseball\) "Uniform number \(Major League Baseball\)") of 99 since it was given to him during 2016 spring training[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-number-288) (higher numbers are typically given to young players who are not expected to make the final regular-season roster). In 2016, Judge stated that he would have preferred either No. 44 ([retired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Major_League_Baseball_retired_numbers "List of Major League Baseball retired numbers") by the Yankees to honor [Reggie Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Jackson "Reggie Jackson")) or No. 35 but was not sure whether he would switch if the latter two were to become available.[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-number-288)
MLB along with the [MLB Players Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Players_Association "Major League Baseball Players Association"), created [Players Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Players_Weekend "Players Weekend") to let players "express themselves while connecting with their past in youth baseball". From August 25–27, 2017, players wore alternate team jerseys inspired by youth league designs. They also had the option to replace their last names with their nicknames on their jersey [nameplates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nameplate "Nameplate"), and the vast majority of players did so. Judge chose the nickname "All Rise" (given to him by former teammate [Todd Frazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Frazier "Todd Frazier")) to be worn on the back of his jersey nameplate.[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-289) For the 2018 Players Weekend, Judge chose to just have his last name on the back of his jersey.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-290) During the 2019 event, Judge chose his own nickname, "BAJ", an abbreviation of "Big Aaron Judge".[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-291)
## Personal life
Judge married his wife in December 2021 at a private ceremony in [Maui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui "Maui").[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-292) They met at [Linden High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linden_High_School_\(California\) "Linden High School \(California\)") and both attended [Fresno State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_University,_Fresno "California State University, Fresno").[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-f687-293) Their first child was born in January 2025.[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-294)
Judge has two pet [dachshunds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dachshund "Dachshund") named Gus and Penny.[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-q364-295)
Judge is a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"). He grew up going to a [Methodist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodist_Christian "Methodist Christian") church and has posted about his faith on his social media accounts.[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-NJ2022-296)[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-297)[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-298)
### Philanthropy
Judge is the founder of the ALL RISE Foundation. Judge's mother, Patty, serves as its executive director and president.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-299) The foundation's mission statement is to "inspire children and youth to become responsible citizens and encourage them to reach unlimited possibilities."[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-300) In January 2024, the foundation hosted an "All-Star Evening" gala on [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street"), raising nearly $800,000 for various youth programs in New York City.[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-301)

In 2024, Judge and his two pet dachshunds guest starred on an episode of _[Rubble& Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubble_&_Crew "Rubble & Crew")_, a _[Paw Patrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paw_Patrol "Paw Patrol")_ spin-off. His wife voiced their dog Penny.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-314)
Judge also participated in the [2026 FIFA World Cup draw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_seeding "2026 FIFA World Cup seeding") on December 5, 2025.[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-315)
On January 27, 2026, Judge was announced as the cover athlete for _[MLB The Show 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_The_Show_26 "MLB The Show 26")_ , becoming just the second player to appear on the game's cover twice.[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-316)
## Career accomplishments
### New York Yankees franchise records
  * Most home runs in a season hit at home: 33 ([Babe Ruth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth") held the record with 32).
  * Most home runs in a season by a rookie: 52 ([Joe DiMaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_DiMaggio "Joe DiMaggio") held the record with 29)[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-317)
  * Most home runs in a single season: 62 ([Roger Maris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Maris "Roger Maris") held the record with 61)[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-318)
  * First right-handed hitter in Yankees history with at least 100 RBIs, 100 runs scored, and 100 walks in a single season
  * Most home runs (4) in the first seven home playoff games, tying [Reggie Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Jackson "Reggie Jackson") (1977–78).
  * Most home runs by the All-Star break (34).[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-h531-319)
  * Fastest to reach 60 home runs in a single season (147th team game).[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-q742-320)
  * First to hit three home runs in a game twice in one season.[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-v249-321)
  * Highest strikeout rate in the postseason (32.8%)
  * Equal most home runs in first 1,000 games with the Yankees: 321 (tied with Babe Ruth)[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Judge#cite_note-:9-234)
